meters.name: application.ready.time
meters.description: Time taken for the application to be ready to service requests

provenance.contributor: Application framework and container instrumentation (Spring Boot, Quarkus, Hibernate, servlet containers, loggers, executors)
provenance.explanation: Time taken for the application to be ready to service requests
provenance.interpretation: These are recorded once per boot, so treat them as a startup budget rather than a live series.

provenance.contributor: Connection-pool instrumentation (HikariCP, Agroal or Micrometer JDBC)
provenance.interpretation: Active, idle and pending are gauges for one pool tag, while the timeout counter accumulates: pending above zero with a maxed active gauge means the pool is exhausted.

provenance.contributor: Framework HTTP server instrumentation (Spring MVC/WebFlux or Quarkus/Vert.x)
provenance.explanation: Timer over inbound HTTP requests, tagged with method, URI template, status and outcome.
provenance.interpretation: Count is requests since start, total is accumulated latency and maximum is the slowest request in the current window; compare per URI template rather than in aggregate.

meters.name: jvm.classes.loaded
meters.description: The number of classes that are currently loaded in the Java virtual machine

provenance.explanation: The number of classes that are currently loaded in the Java virtual machine
provenance.interpretation: The loaded gauge is instantaneous while the unloaded counter accumulates, so continuous growth in both hints at dynamic class generation.

meters.name: jvm.gc.overhead
meters.description: An approximation of the percent of CPU time used by GC activities over the last lookback period or since monitoring began, whichever is shorter, in the range [0..1]

provenance.explanation: An approximation of the percent of CPU time used by GC activities over the last lookback period or since monitoring began, whichever is shorter, in the range [0..1]
provenance.interpretation: The pause timer's count is the number of collections since start, its total the accumulated pause time and its maximum the worst pause in the current window.

provenance.contributor: Messaging client instrumentation (Kafka, RabbitMQ/AMQP or JMS)
provenance.explanation: Kafka producer, consumer and listener throughput, lag and timing.
provenance.interpretation: The Kafka client mixes cumulative totals with client-computed rate gauges, so check the base unit and prefer the total when comparing intervals.

meters.name: ledger.audit.dead_lettered
meters.description: Records parked on ledger.events.DLT by the audit consumer (spec §6.6)

provenance.explanation: Records parked on ledger.events.DLT by the audit consumer (spec §6.6)

provenance.contributor: Application framework and container instrumentation (Spring Boot, Quarkus, Hibernate, servlet containers, loggers, executors)
provenance.explanation: Authentication, authorization and filter-chain timings from Spring Security.
provenance.interpretation: Counters are tagged by outcome and authentication type: a rising failure count with a steady total usually means credential problems rather than load.

groups.label: JVM
groups.summary: Memory pools, garbage collection, threads, class loading and buffer pools reported by the JVM itself.
groups.interpretation: Gauges are point-in-time readings, while counters and timers accumulate for the whole process lifetime, so read them as totals since start rather than as a current rate.

groups.label: System
groups.summary: Host-level CPU, load average and disk space visible to the JVM.
groups.interpretation: These gauges describe the machine rather than the application, so compare them against process gauges before blaming the application for host-wide pressure.

groups.label: Application / unclassified
groups.summary: Meters whose names match no known integration convention. They are usually registered by this application or by a library BootUI does not recognize.
groups.interpretation: BootUI does not invent documentation for these meters: any description shown here comes from the registry itself, and an absent description simply means none was registered.
